name: Missouri

law.summary: Every permitted wastewater facility must report SSOs and bypasses to DNR within 24 hours through MoGEM; no duty to tell the public was found and DNR publishes nothing. Public notice is consent-decree or utility practice (signs).

citations.cite: Missouri DNR sewer overflow guidance (permit standard conditions)
citations.title: Sanitary Sewer Overflows
citations.quote: All permitted wastewater treatment facilities must report SSOs or bypasses from their treatment works or collection system to the department within 24 hours of discovering the event.

citations.title: State park beach bacteria standard
citations.quote: If beaches exceed the GM standard established in subsection 1 of this section, the department of natural resources shall post the beach with signs that state "Swimming is Not Recommended".
citations.threshold: geometric mean 190 E. coli/100 mL (per search)

regulator_report.cite: DNR guidance; permit standard conditions (10 CSR 20 not fetched)

bills_and_cases: MSD St. Louis consent decree (2011, Project Clear).
Kansas City consent decree (2010, Smart Sewer).
No 2025-2026 bill on sewage public notice found (search only).

erule.notes: MoGEM; no public output; no MO rows in SOBE.

statewide_feed.notes: MoGEM reports are not published; records by Sunshine Law request.

cso.notification_practice: Signs at outfalls (MSD, KC Water); press releases for some large SSOs (KC Water); MSD site behind a bot wall.

sso.notes: KC Water press releases name street addresses.

beaches.program: Missouri DNR weekly E. coli sampling at state park beaches (Memorial Day to Labor Day), signs and online status, email sign-up
beaches.notes: HAB closures handled separately (Pomme de Terre).

watershed_groups: Missouri Coalition for the Environment (not checked)

outfalls.cso_inventory_gap: large: MSD Lemay 120 CSO outfalls in the state layer vs 0 open in EPA; MSD Bissell Point CSOs in neither; KC Blue River 80 in EPA but not flagged in the state layer

barriers.note: DNR could publish its MoGEM table as Tennessee does.

barriers.what: msdprojectclear.org (MSD St. Louis) and kcsmartsewer.us block automated access
CSO notice is by outfall signs
Overflow reports via Sunshine Law request

subscriptions.name: Missouri DNR GovDelivery
subscriptions.what: beach status and other DNR topics

readiness.rationale: No public event data: MoGEM is closed, MSD's site is bot-walled and KC Water only posts occasional press releases. The state outfall layer is valuable because it puts MSD's 120 Lemay CSOs on the map; Bissell Point still needs locating. Beaches (state parks) are the only dated advisories.

owner_questions: Request MSD St. Louis's CSO outfall list (Bissell Point) and ask whether it has a notification page behind the bot wall?
Ask Missouri DNR whether MoGEM SSO data can be published (Tennessee is the model)?
Subscribe to Missouri DNR beach status email?
surprise: The EPA national CSO inventory shows St. Louis MSD, one of the largest combined systems in the country, with zero open CSO outfalls; Missouri's own layer has 120 for Lemay alone, and Bissell Point's are in neither.
